thread.title: Apple enters correction territory for second time this year

author: morningstar.com
title: Apple enters correction territory for second time this year
text:
Apple Inc. (AAPL) closed in correction territory for the second time this year on Tuesday. Shares closed at $162.94, down 10.3% from its March 12 closing high of $181.72. A decline of 10% from a high is defined as a correction (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/was-that-a-stock-market-crash-do-the-math-and-check-the-yield-curve-2018-02-06). Apple experienced a correction earlier this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-stock-suffers-first-official-correction-in-15-months-2018-02-02), amid a tough February for tech stocks, but then rose to the new record high in March to climb out of the previous correction (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stop-saying-the-dow-is-moving-in-and-out-of-correction-that-is-not-how-stock-market-moves-work-2018-03-23). Apple is set to report earnings May 1, and has been beset by doubts about iPhone sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-falls-after-analysts-express-caution-ahead-of-earnings-2018-04-20). Apple stock has declined 3.7% so far this year, as the S&P 500 index has declined 0.1%. Shares declined 1.4% in Tuesday's session as stocks struggled overall (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-shapes-up-to-break-losing-streak-but-earnings-could-kill-the-buzz-2018-04-24).
-Jeremy C. Owens; 1642ET
